title: Jobs that make you happy

fn.en: Talk about jobs and ask yes/no questions about work.

useful: Yes, he does. / No, he doesn’t.

items.a: My son fixes a lot of machines
Manu takes pictures with his camera
My brother flies planes for an airline
Sameeha cleans and fixes people’s teeth

items.q: I never go to the office. I work from ___.
I have no boss and no company. I work ___.
I only work Monday and Tuesday. I work ___.
The money you get every month is your ___.
The people you work with are your ___.
Too much work and no time. The job is very ___.

sub.en: Look at the questions. Which word carries the tense — do/does, or the main verb?

items.why: does carries the -s, so the main verb goes back to its base form: Does he work…?

items.q: Does she ___ in a big office?

items.why: A question with is takes is in the answer; a question with does takes does.

items.q: She’s ___ engineer and her brother is ___ pilot.

Does your boss earn a lot

acts.title: Three people who like Mondays
text: Máté works at a cinema, but he doesn’t sell tickets. He is the piano player. His cinema shows old silent films, so it needs someone to play the music. He watches the film and decides what to play: slow music for a sad part, fast music for an exciting one. The salary isn’t big, but he doesn’t want another job.

Dana is a fire lookout. She works alone in a forest and her office is a small wooden room at the top of a tower. She doesn’t work in a big office and she doesn’t have colleagues. She enjoys it. “People think it is boring,” she says. “It isn’t.”
Nurlan is a hairdresser. He works freelance and goes to people’s homes. He works part-time, so he earns less than his friends, but his job isn’t stressful and he finishes at three.

items.s: Máté sells tickets at the cinema.
Máté plays fast music for a sad part of a film.
Dana works with a lot of colleagues.

write.q: Write about your job and one other person’s: 6 sentences. Say what you do, where you work, whether you work full-time or part-time, and whether you enjoy it. Then write two yes/no questions you would ask a new colleague.
write.model: I’m an engineer and I work for a small company in Almaty. I work full-time, from nine to six. I enjoy my job, but it’s sometimes stressful. My sister is a hairdresser — she works freelance and goes to people’s homes. Do you work from home? Does your company pay a good salary?

speak.q: Interview a partner out loud: What do you do? Do you work full-time? Do you work from home? Do you enjoy your job? Then answer the same questions with full short answers.
speak.model: What do you do? — I’m a nurse. Do you work full-time? — Yes, I do. Do you work from home? — No, I don’t. Do you enjoy your job? — Yes, I do, but it’s stressful.
